verdict.rationale: PostHog documents autonomous background work: it turns product signals into researched reports and pull requests delivered to an Inbox for review. It also offers real-time data destinations and scheduled flag changes, but the evidence does not show users defining their own custom AI automations or triggers. Scheduled flag changes are one-off actions, not recurring schedules. missing for 10: documentation on configuring user-defined autonomous automations (triggers, recurring schedules, actions), depth of the signals-to-PR agent, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Turn signals in your product data (errors, rage clicks, failed queries, and more) into researched reports and pull requests, delivered to your Inbox for you to review and merge.
Review proposed improvements and pull requests, then decide what ships.
Send it to 25+ tools or any webhook in real time, or batch export large amounts to your warehouse.
Create flags, set release conditions, schedule changes, and watch rollouts land.
